report:
Not built: the cache conflicts with a recorded owner decision, so I stopped to ask first.

The request: add a small cache to get_price so basket_total runs faster.

The conflict: docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-09-02, says "No caching layer in the price service. Every call to get_price reads the live price." The reason given: prices change every minute, and a cached price once sold stock at an old price and caused a round of refunds. The owner made that decision. A cache on get_price breaks it directly.

No files were changed.

Choices for you to pick from:
1. Keep the decision. Speed up basket_total without a cache on get_price. Look up each distinct SKU once per basket_total call (for example, 10 apples cost one lookup, not 10). Every get_price call still reads live. A basket with N items and K distinct SKUs then needs K backend calls instead of N, about 300 ms each.
2. Keep the decision. Add a batch lookup (one backend call for many SKUs) if the pricing backend supports one. I have not seen a batch API in this repo.
3. Change the decision. Add the cache to get_price as asked, with a short life (for example, under one minute), and record the new decision in docs/DECISIONS.md. This brings back the stale price risk that the decision was made to stop.

Tell me which one to build.
